articleTitle: A Novel Three-Port Converter for Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: The demand for renewable energy has been steadily increasing since the start of this century. As a result, energy storage to overcome the intermittency of the renewable energy sources is also on the rise. Therefore, Three-Port Converters (TPCs), which interface a Photovoltaic (PV) panel, a bidirectional battery, and a load port have attracted more and more research. Meanwhile, Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) is an increasingly popular power transfer technology. The mainstream WPT technology is Inductive Power Transfer (IPT), which transfers energy by magnetic coupling of inductive coils. WPT is widely used in EV/UAV charging and some other charging scenarios. In this paper, a novel three-port converter for outdoor wireless charging is proposed based on the characteristics of Wireless Power Transfer (WPT). Furthermore, the derivation of the proposed topology is discussed based on the analysis of power flow. Finally, the basic modulation strategies of all the working modes are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Optimization of Differential Class E Inverter for Lower EMI
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: Single-switch resonant inverters are widely used due to their simple circuit topology and low cost, and Class E inverter is the most widely used topology among them. However, the output sensitivity of Class E inverter limits the applications. This paper aims at optimizing the design process of single-switch resonant converters by frequency-based extended impedance method (EIM), and finding the design points which make the total harmonic distortion (THD) of the waveforms smaller. After optimization, the electromagnetic interference on the output side would be reduced and the output waveforms would be more sinusoidal.

articleTitle: Effect of Rebar Array on IPT System for Structural Health Monitoring Sensor Supply
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: Inductive power transfer (IPT) has become a popular supply of sensors in structural health monitoring systems due to its non-contact nature. However, the presence of a rebar array in concrete structures may affect the performance of IPT systems by changing the mutual inductance between the transmitter and receiver coils. Moreover, as a ferromagnetic material, the relative permeability of rebar is a complex function of frequency. In this paper, the approximate relative permeability of rebars at different frequencies is obtained by inductance approximation of finite element simulation and test results. Based on this, we study the influence of the magnetic properties of rebars and eddy current shielding on mutual inductance through simulation and testing. The results indicate that the eddy current shielding effect of rebar loops plays a dominant role in reducing mutual inductance within the frequency range commonly used in IPT systems. An expression for the equivalent mutual inductance of IPT systems with rebars is also derived and validated with experimental results. An expression for the equivalent mutual inductance of IPT systems with rebar array is also derived and validated with experimental results. The findings of this study are expected to assist in designing IPT systems in the presence of rebar obstructions.

articleTitle: Transmitting Coil Array Optimization for Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: A 10 cm by 10 cm transmitting coil is designed for an inductive power transfer system 5×5 coil array. The coil is a spiral coil, and the transmitting coil has the same size as the receiving coil, and the geometry of transmitting coil is optimized to ensure an even magnetic field distribution on the receiving side. Define the disturbance of magnetic field in a certain transmitting area, and the optimization is to enlarge the transmitting area at the same disturbance, by optimizing the transmitting coil structure. As a result, the optimization shows 7.35 % uniformity rise from original coil. This uniformity guarantees a uniform power delivery regardless of the position of the receiving side.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Distributed Consensus Based Economic Dispatch of Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) for Networked Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: Rapid inclusion of distributed energy resources (DERs) has led to the need for a reliable energy management system (EMS) capable of managing these resources effectively at a large scale. This paper proposes a novel hierarchical distributed consensus-based approach for solving the economic dispatch problem in networked microgrids (NMGs). The proposed approach arranges the network in hierarchical structure, thereby reducing the communication requirement between the distributed controllers. Simulation results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. The simulation involves comparing the proposed approach with distributed consensus approach for different network topologies.

articleTitle: Performance Assessment of Capacitive Power Transfer in Water with Varied Conductivity
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: This paper investigates two types of insulated capacitive couplers, parallel and stacked, that can be applied to underwater capacitive power transfer (CPT). The two four-plate capacitive couplers are sealed into an insulating medium to reduce the additional losses caused by ion displacement currents when transmitting electrical energy in underwater electric fields. Finite element analysis using 3D RLCG extraction tool Q3D was performed to simulate the coupling parameters of the couplers. The variation law of coupling parameters of couplers in water with different conductivity was studied using and it was found that parallel insulated couplers have good potential for application in high conductivity water. At the same time, the misalignment tolerance of the coupler in different conductivity water media is analyzed, and the coupling parameters are little affected by the parallel movement of the pole plate, and the coupler still has good anti-misalignment performance in the x-y plane. The prototype design of the CPT system uses the above two insulated couplers, and the performance of the system in high conductivity water environment is initially verified by using circuit simulation software.

articleTitle: Two-Port Measurement of Packaging Parasitic Inductance in SiC Half-Bridge Power Modules Considering Mutual Inductance*
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: This paper proposed a two-port measurement method, which improves the accuracy of measured parasitic inductances for SiC MOSFET half-bridge modules by considering the mutual inductances. The method process has three steps to measure the impedance parameters (Z-parameters) by imitating the switching transient. Then, the model of the power module was simulated in ANSYS Q3D to extract the parasitic inductances including the mutual inductances. These parameters were imported to ADS to build the small signal model of the SiC MOSFET. The proposed method was applied to the simulation circuit, and the ADS results agree well with the Q3D results, showing a maximum error of 0.9%. The validation indicates that the proposed measurement method can extract parasitic inductance accurately through the simple three steps.

articleTitle: Virtual Verification and Validation for Sustainable Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: The concept of sustainable manufacturing (SM) is discussed, recent development on enabling technologies for SM are surveyed to identify promising research subjects, and virtual verification and validation (V&V) is focused to enhance the sustainability of small and medium sized enterprises (SMEs). A case-study computer aided engineering (CAE) system has been developed to reduce the needs of physical prototyping and tests in product developments. The effectiveness of the prototyped system is elaborated in terms of (1) significant savings from replacing numerous physical experiments by virtual tests, (2) shortened design cycles, and (3) the possibility of exploring a large design space for product optimization. The improvements at all these aspects contribute to system sustainability greatly.

articleTitle: A Novel Simultaneous Wireless Power and Data Transfer Scheme for Two-stage Inductive Power Transfer Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: Simultaneous wireless power and data transfer (SWPDT) is proposed to realize the functions including closed-loop control, state monitoring, instruction delivering, and information exchange in inductive power transfer systems. However, the significant interference from power transfer to data transfer (P2D interference) limits the practical implementation of SWPDT. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a novel SWPDT scheme. The data is not transferred in the transition stages of the power switches. A dedicated frame header and end are designed to demodulate the data correctly in the receiving side. The proposed SWPDT scheme is verified by simulation. The output power is 11.1 kW while the data transfer rate is 1.6 Mbps. No bit error is observed, validating the reliability of the proposed SWPDT scheme.

IEEE Keywords: Simultaneous wireless information and power transfer
Author Keywords: simultaneous wireless power and data transfer (SWPDT)

articleTitle: Sliding Mode-Based Active Disturbance Rejection Control of Doubly Salient PM Generator-Based Tidal Stream Turbine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: A low-speed high torque Doubly Salient Permanent Magnet Generator (DSPMG), in this paper, is adopted for renewable energy generation. Nevertheless, this machine has strong nonlinearity and coupling, which lead to a large torque ripple. Therefore, to reduce the torque ripple and improve the speed response, and makes the system stably. Sliding Mode -based Active Disturbance Rejection Control (SM-ADRC) and Iterative Learning Control (ILC) are proposed for speed and current loop of this system respectively. According to the simulation results, the proposed SM-ADRC + ILC strategy has the best speed response and lowest torque ripples, and strong robustness.

Author Keywords: sliding mode-based active disturbance rejection control

articleTitle: Real-Time Energy Storage System Control Strategies for Urban Rail Transit with Renewable Energy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: The energy storage system (ESS) and renewable energy source (RES) have been applied in some urban rail transit (URT), aiming to reduce energy consumption from the utility grid. However, the SOC of ESS highly affects the performance of ESS in supporting urban rail transit. Thus, this research proposes a real-time control strategy of ESS in urban rail transit with RES, which can dynamically control substations to charge ESS to support the peak shaving function of ESS. The mathematic model of the URT and ESS was established first. Then, the power flow method of URT with ESS and RES is introduced to analyze the energy distribution. Besides, a real-time SOC control strategy is designed to ensure ESS has enough stored energy to shave the peak power of the substation. The case study based on the Merseyrail line shows that the proposed real-time SOC control strategy can remain the SOC of ESS above the target value.

articleTitle: Crossing Power Restraint under Bidirectional Traction Substation Converter in Urban Rail Transit with Multiple Reflux Paths Coupling
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: At present, the catenaries and running rails of urban transit are connected in the whole line respectively. Due to the parallel operation of multiple trains, crossing power is generated inevitably between power supply sections of the traction substations which will increase rail potential amplitude. Although crossing power energy absorption methods have been gradually studied, the analysis of crossing power restrain effect based on output characteristics of bidirectional converter in traction substation is still lacking. In this paper, the model of DC traction power supply system of urban rail transit with bidirectional traction substation converter and multiple reflux paths coupling is established. Then, taking Guangzhou Metro Line 2 as an example, the effect of output characteristics optimization on restraining crossing power is studied, rail potential with different output characteristics and return path coupling is compared. Results show that, rail potential will be reduced by crossing power restraint based on the characteristics optimization of bidirectional converter.

articleTitle: Research On the Coordinated Operation and Energy Saving of Reversible Converter and Rectifier Unit
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: For the regenerative braking energy(RBE) in the urban rail transit, the reversible converter can effectively enhance the utilization of RBE and also can replace the rectifier units(RU). However, it is necessary to study the coordinated scheme of reversible converter and RU because of high cost of large-capacity reversible converter. This paper analyzes the comprehensive output external characteristics under different working conditions of coordinated scheme, proposed the state switching strategy in power supply calculation, and analyzes the influence of control parameters of reversible converter on energy saving. The simulation results show that the power loss of the system is reduced applying the coordinated scheme with proper parameters, thus the energy saving effect is improved. This research can provide reference for the optimal operation and energy-saving effect evaluation of coordinated scheme.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of Rectifier Impedance Characteristics of IPT System with S/SP Compensation Topology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: In the inductive power transfer (IPT) system with S/SP compensation topology, the LC filter rectifier is affected by harmonics, which makes the input impedance of the rectifier non-resistive. In this paper, the structure and parameters of the S/SP compensation topology are analyzed and designed, which can keep the rectifier impedance purely resistive in a wider load range. Firstly, the impedance characteristics of the traditional rectifier is analyzed, and the accurate circuit model is established. Then, based on traditional analysis, the parameters and model of novel S/SP compensation topology are analyzed and designed, and the input impedance angle of the rectifier is zero. Finally, a prototype of the novel S/SP compensation topology is built to validate the proposed method. MOSFETs always implement ZVS.

articleTitle: Collaborative Control Strategy Design of Photovoltaic Energy Storage and DC Microgrid for Electric Vehicles Using Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: Using wireless power transfer (WPT) technology to supply power to electric vehicles (EVs) has the advantages of safety, convenience, and high degree of automation. Furthermore, considering the use of photovoltaic (PV) and storage DC microgrids as energy inputs, it can avoid the impact of EV charging on the power grid. Based on this, a collaborative control strategy for WPT of EVs and PV and storage microgrid is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the working characteristics of the PV power generation system, energy storage system, and WPT system for EVs are analyzed, and the circuit models for each link is constructed. Next, the energy supply relationship between the multiple links is studied and designed, and an energy management strategy based on constant DC bus voltage is proposed. The PV power generation system adopts maximum power point tracking (MPPT) control. When there is surplus energy, the energy storage system absorbs the excess energy, and when there is insufficient energy, the energy storage system fills the energy gap. Finally, a 30 kW EV power supply system is simulated to verify the feasibility of the proposed topology and the effectiveness of the control strategy.

articleTitle: Accelerated Aging Test Method of Lithium-Ion Batteries Featured with Aging Feature Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: Accelerated aging test (AAT) is required to efficiently evaluate the operating life of lithium-ion batteries (LiB). It can partially substitute traditional aging test which typically lasts for thousands of LiB charge/discharge cycles. A practical AAT should consider the operation condition features (OCF) in its aging models, such as charge/discharge rate, ambient temperature, ampere-hour throughput and the time distribution of current rate (TDOCR). This paper proposes a new AAT method for optimizing both reduction in test time and TDOCR reconstruction. An algorithm is designed to ensure the OCF equivalence of the AAT profile and the operating profile. The limitations of aging stress threshold and the retention of TDOCR are mainly considered, and addressed by the segmented equal scaling method (SESM) of feature reconstruction. Based on the aging model featured by the Arrhenius formula, the validity of the method is verified with typical FUDS profile and NEDC profile.

articleTitle: Development of Ultimate Drive System for Electric Vehicles: Wireless Power Transfer integrated In-Wheel Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: GHG(Green House Gas) emission by internal combustion engines is one of the biggest environmental issues of vehicles. Electric vehicles (EVs) are marketed in recent years due to their high environmental performance, and the share of EVs in the market grows year by year.

articleTitle: An Energy Control Strategy in Hybrid Electric Ships Considering the Battery Life
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: Considering the effect of battery life on the full-life-cycle cost of hybrid electric ships (HES), an energy control strategy has been proposed, with the minimization of fuel consumption and battery's health degradation as the optimization objective. Firstly, the double-objectives cost function is established based the diesel engine fuel consumption model, power battery internal resistance model and battery life model. Then, the dynamic programming (DP) algorithm is employed to achieve the global optimization and the optimal weight coefficient is selected according to the optimization results. The experimental results show that, compared with the control strategy based on the single-objective optimization of fuel consumption or the control strategy based on fuzzy logic, the proposed strategy can reduce the fuel consumption and further extend the battery life, and it has good feasibility and practicality.

articleTitle: Robust Wireless Power Transfer via Topological Dimer Chain
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) applications are becoming increasingly widespread, with the popularity of various electronic products and electric vehicles. In this paper, we proposed a topological dimer chain WPT system which can transfer power over a long distance with coils in a chain. At the same time, the unique topological edge mode in this structure can make the system highly robust to external disturbances. This system provides new ideas for improving the efficiency and security of WPT.

articleTitle: Closed-Form Solutions of Mutual Inductance and Load for LCC-S Wireless Power Transfer Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) technology has gained significant attention in recent years due to its potential to revolutionize the way to charge and power electronic devices. Accurate estimation of mutual inductance and load resistance are essential to achieve control goals as well as optimal operation of the system. This paper proposes an approach to obtain analytical closed-form solution of mutual inductance and load resistance for the LCC-S compensated WPT system, without communication from the receiver side. It also analyzes the sensitivity of the estimation results to both measurements and other system parameters. The results of simulation and hardware experiments confirm the feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Current Status and Issues of DWPT and ERS in Japan
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: Recent study and development of DWPT and ERS in Japan are reviewed. Current evaluation issues and future challenges for social implementation are introduced. Important safety issue utilizing control and communication is proposed for international standard. This paper also reviews history and recent trend of Static WPT and Electric Road System(ERS) based on DWPT in Japan. Review current status and activity from Japan of standardization and regulatory such as ISO, IEC,SAE,ITU and CISPR. Report on ongoing challenge plan in Japan using test course for innovative ERS featuring Magnetic or Capacitive Coupling DWPT including at Fiji-Yoshida city is introduced. They will contribute carbon free smart mobility society in the future expected 2050 in Japan. It will also introduced the plan of Fujisan railway which was reported by Fujisan railway study committee at Feb.2021. The draft plan of Fujisan railway with no catenary LRT (expected by using DWPT) are overviewed.

articleTitle: MPC2 Energy Router: Model Predictive Control Method for Magnetic-Coupled Multi-Port Power Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: Magnetic-coupled multi-port power converter (MPC converter) shows great potential as an energy router for the future energy Internet. However, the challenge of regulating power flow and voltage across different ports presents a significant hurdle, as there is inherent cross-coupling. This paper proposes a model predictive control (MPC control) method for MPC converters. First, the multi-input multi-output small signal state space model is established to predict future behavior. Second, an optimization problem is solved based on the predictive model, and the control law is obtained. Finally, a 6-ports 300W <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$MPC^{2}$</tex> energy router prototype, consisting of an MPC converter board and an MPC control board, is built to verify the proposed MPC control method, and the abilities of command tracking and disturbance rejection are tested.

articleTitle: Research on Optimal Scheduling Considering the Integration of Source-Network-Load-Storage Coordination in Extreme Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: With the continuous development of new energy, the massive grid-connection of renewable energy had also brought new challenges to the stable operation of the power system. When the grid is extremely unstable, it's necessary to mobilize all controllable resources, relying on the coordinated operation the power supply side, grid side, and load side, that is, the integrated operation of “source-network-load-storage” to ensure the safety and stability of the system. This paper first establishes the energy model of wind-solar-storage and cooling-heating power equipment in the integrated energy system. Then, from the perspective of intelligent interaction among source, network, load and storage, considers the power demand response and heat demand response in extreme cases, and establishes the optimal scheduling model of load-side resources participating in power grid balance. Finally, the objective function is established with the goal of minimizing the daily comprehensive operating cost of the integrated energy system, and the particle swarm algorithm is used to optimize and solve the objective function. The results of the example show that the method can realize the economic operation of the integrated energy system under extreme conditions, reduce the emission of carbon dioxide, and promote the consumption of new energy.

articleTitle: A Common Ground Switched-Capacitor Multilevel Inverter Using Capacitors of Small Value and Featuring a Continuous Input Current
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: A new input source - load common ground switched-capacitor multilevel inverter (CG - SCMLI) with superior features is proposed. The first goal is to assure a continuous input current despite the creation of the common ground that, in the available solutions, prevented the input source of supplying energy when synthesizing the negative levels of the staircase output voltage, creating thus discontinuities in the input current. The availability of a common ground and of a low pulsating input current are the two qualities provided by the new inverter which fit exactly the requirements of the photovoltaics cells used to power the energy grid. A charge pump cell is used for assuring the new feature of the input current, but also for allowing a design with much smaller capacitors, that is the second goal of this research. Even if the proposed inverter contains more switches than the available CG-SCMLIs, the above qualities gives the superiority of the new solution. A prototype of 200 W supplied by an array of solar cells of MPPT voltage 120V is implemented in the laboratory. It uses capacitors of 32.9 µF, which gives a high power density to the prototype. The new 7 - levels inverter supplies a voltage of 220 Vrms to a standalone consumer. The measured efficiency is 97.4%.

articleTitle: A Multi-Layer Long Short-Term Memory Neural Network on Battery State-of-Health Estimation with Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: Due to the important part of batteries in industrial systems, its safety analysis has causes widespread attention from researchers, and its effective maintenance decision-making is needed. Data-driven state-of-health (SOH) estimation can provide useful information by monitoring historical data during the aging process, but it can be failed in the cross-domain scenarios due to the different data distributions. To tackle this issue, we propose a long short-term memory (LSTM) neural network with an additional fully connected dense as a basic predictor, and apply the pretrain and fine-tuning training algorithm to realize the high-performance prediction. By validated in two real-world datasets, we find that blindly expanding the training set may have a negative impact on model accuracy, and the proposed TL-LSTM can achieve a great performance under the cross-domain tasks.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of DC Capacitance of Photovoltaic Self-Synchronizing Voltage Source
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: The self-synchronous voltage source inverter is similar in external characteristics to a synchronous generator and has an excellent performance in frequency and voltage regulation. In the scenario of grid-forming, the output power of the photovoltaic self-synchronizing voltage source is insufficient due to the inherent intermittent light disturbance, which is easy to cause DC undervoltage and even system shutdown accidents. DC capacitor energy storage can bear the output power shortage during light disturbance for a short time, provide sufficient time support for inverter output power regulation, and avoid undervoltage accidents. For this reason, this paper proposes an optimal design method of capacitance parameters based on the DC voltage transient model. This method realizes the accurate description of DC voltage fluctuations based on the inverter transient model, establishes the numerical relationship between lighting disturbance and DC voltage fluctuations under different capacitance parameters, and finally realizes the optimal design of capacitance. The simulation results show that the proposed method can provide 100-millisecond support for the inverter output power regulation during the light disturbance, effectively alleviate the DC voltage drop, and improve the DC side voltage stability of the inverter.

articleTitle: Current Sources and Actual PV Modules based Photovoltaic (PV) Emulator for Testing MPPT Algorithms and PV Inverters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: PV array emulator has been widely used for testing PV inverters and their control algorithms such as maximum power point tracking (MPPT) algorithms. Various power electronics converter-based PV emulators have been presented in many research papers. This paper presents a PV emulator that is based on indoor solar panels (without solar irradiance) and external current source (dc power supply). The external current source is used to emulate the photo current that is usually generated by solar panel under sunlight. The advantages of the proposed PV emulator are that it can generate similar electrical characteristics of actual PV panel without sunlight, it is suitable for testing PV inverters and MPPT algorithms in indoor conditions where the sunlight is usually very weak. In addition, a PV array emulator that can emulate electrical performance under partial shading conditions was constructed by using two solar panels and two current sources. Test results show that the proposed PV emulator provides a similar performance of real PV array under real sun light. It provides a low-cost solution for testing PV inverters and control algorithms inside a laboratory environment.

articleTitle: Overload Evaluation of MV Distribution Lines based on Thermal Inertia Characteristics under High Penetration of DERs
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: To realize a carbon-neutral society, integrating distributed energy resources (DERs), such as photovoltaic systems (PVs) and electric vehicles (EVs), into distribution networks is imperative. As PV generations and EV charging loads have been increasingly used as DERs, the line current in medium-voltage distribution networks experiences increased fluctuations. This study evaluates overloading in overhead distribution cables based on a conductor temperature model that addresses the high penetration of PV generation and charging loads. The cable conductor temperature model is based on the thermal-electrical equivalent circuit model. Under highly fluctuated line current variations that are attributable to the actual monitored solar irradiation data, distribution line overload is evaluated by considering the thermal inertia of the conductor temperature.

articleTitle: Multi-Frequency Damping Adaptive Control Strategy for Active Dampers Based on MultiHarmonic Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: As the interface between new energy and the power grid, grid-connected converters are easy to cause multifrequency oscillation of the system. So, this paper proposes an active damper to dampen multiple harmonics by simulating virtual resistance. The basic idea of the active damper is that use the cascaded multiple Second-Order Generalized Integrator with the Frequency-Locked Loops (SOGI-FLL) to detect and extract the unknown multiple harmonics automatically. Then, for different content of resonance, the active damper adjusts the virtual resistance value adaptively to enhance the stability of the system. Finally, the simulations of MATLAB/Simulink are carried out and the results verify the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Study of Canceling Onboard Braking Resistance in Urban Rail
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: The utilization of regenerative braking energy (RBE) has attracted lots of studies. The onboard braking resistance (OBR) can consume RBE, but RBE will be wasted. With the development of RBE utilization devices like energy feedback system (EFS), the canceling of OBR is the general trend in the future design of urban rail. To accurately simulate the system, the AC/DC power flow calculation algorithm is improved, and it can be applied in the system with and without OBR. A sample case is studied. First, the accuracy of the algorithm is verified through the field test. Then, the single-pair departure and high-density departure scenarios are studied. The results show that when EFSs are installed at each traction substation, the rail voltage is in the safe range when OBR is canceled.

articleTitle: Graphene Composite for Supercapacitor and Battery Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: Graphene offers a new opportunity to boost the performance of energy storage for supercapacitors and batteries. However, the individual graphene sheets tend to restack due to the van der Waals forces between them, which often cause significant decrease in the electrochemical active surface area as well as the inter-graphene channels accessible to the electrolyte ions. To tackle these issues, we have explored and developed several strategies including adoption of single-walled carbon nanotubes (CNTs) and ionic liquids as spacers for graphene sheets in order to reduce their agglomeration. We found that the electrochemical properties of the graphene/CNT composite electrode were indeed much improved. The two-dimensional graphene nanosheets have also been successfully assembled into hollow spheres using polystyrene spheres as a template. Compared with traditional graphene materials, the as-prepared graphene hollow spheres can produce more free space between them to result in a larger accessible surface area for ion adsorption. The electrochemical characterization of our recent graphene supercapacitors and battery applications will be presented. These materials have been successfully applied in the development of graphene supercapacitors for industrial applications through our venture technology company.

articleTitle: Plasma Absorption Techniques in Direct Current Circuit Breakers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: DC circuit breakers are becoming popular in the industry with the renewable energy demand. Compared to AC circuit breaking, DC circuit breaking needs an advanced method to immobilize the arc generated during the opening process of the circuit breaker. These days, AC circuit breakers are used with simple modifications for DC circuit breaking. Commercial parties simply modify the AC circuit breakers to operate on DC. However, specifically manufactured DC circuit breakers are necessary for the long run as modified versions still have minimum cycle life due to contact point degradation compared to commercially available AC circuit breakers. This paper proposes a new concept for DC circuit breakers where a supercapacitor will be used to absorb the arc energy to extend its cycle life.

articleTitle: Power Control Strategy for Cascaded 3L-NPC Converters Considering Thermal Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: Cascaded three-level neutral-point-clamped (C3L-NPC) converters have been recently adopted in medium-voltage direct-current (MVDC) distribution networks, such as in the ANGLE-DC project in North Wales, UK. Compared with its counterpart MMCs, the C3L-NPC converters' main advantage is the much lower cost. This paper presents a power control strategy for this type of converter considering junction temperature conditions. Firstly, a power control loop with a DC voltage balancing controller is presented, to control the output power and stabilize the DC voltages of submodules (SMs) concurrently. Then, a thermal regulation method is proposed considering the unbalanced thermal stresses among SMs. By means of thermal regulation, the thermal stresses are equally shared among SMs, which enhances the system reliability. A system model which includes both the electrical and thermal elements is presented. The parameter tuning of the controllers is performed based on the system pole placement. The effectiveness of the proposed control strategies is finally verified by PLECS simulation and experimental tests.

articleTitle: A Lithium-Ion Battery Group AC Self-Heating Approach Based on Multi-Active-Bridge Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: Lithium-ion battery is playing an increasingly important role as an energy storage system in today's power systems. Pre-heating of the Lithium-ion is significant for the operation safety and state of health, when the operation temperature is really low. This paper analyzes the impedance model of Lithium-ion batteries, selects the frequency of pure ohmic resistance as the frequency of the AC heating current, and proposes a method for self-heating the AC current generated by the Multi-Active-Bridge (MAB) converter. Finally, a 4-port MAB converter is established to verify the above self-heating mechanism.

articleTitle: AdaBoost-Based Cyberattack Detection Algorithm for Battery Systems Providing Frequency Regulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: The intermittent nature of renewable energy sources may require the integration of an increasing amount of battery energy storage systems (BESSs) in the electrical grid. A BESS can provide multiple services such as frequency regulation and backup. Simultaneously, internet-of-things (IoT) enabled technologies are increasingly being applied in the BESS domain. IoT integration is not supported by any specific regulations with respect to BESS design and operation, which can increase the vulnerability of utility-scale batteries to cyberattacks. Cyberattacks can compromise the ability of BESSs to provide an adequate and reliable response to the system's demand. This paper presents a machine-learning-based algorithm for cyberattack detection that can decrease the vulnerability of a BESS to cyber threats. It utilizes Adaptive Boosting to forecast the state of charge and detect potentially corrupted data. Moreover, this paper presents mathematical models of cyberattacks than can be applied against a BESS, providing frequency regulation. The benefits of applying the novel cyberattack detection algorithm are demonstrated in the example of the simulated dataset. The dataset is generated based on parameters of the largest grid-connected BESS in Denmark as well as real frequency data of the Nordic Region.

articleTitle: Torque Distribution Control of Trains Equipped with Driven Independently Rotating Wheels for Guidance Control and Adhesion Control
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: This paper presents a torque distribution control of trains with driven independently rotating wheels. The control strategy makes full use of motors to achieve traction function and guidance function. Besides, the adhesion limit is considered. The concept of normal operation priority is applied in torque distribution. It means that avoidind trains idling/sliding has the highest priority, which is achieved by the adhesion control. The guidance control also gives the torque commands of left motors and right motors. Then, torque distribution rules are designed based on the wheel-rail adhesion state to realize the coordination of guidance control and adhesion control. The MATLAB/Simulink-SIMPACK co-simulation results show that the train runs safely with different wheel-rail adhesion conditions and guidance function is achieved. The proposed control strategy ensures train steering, traction and braking performance.

articleTitle: A Gate Driver for Fast Switching and EMI Suppression of Cascode GaN-Based Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: Due to the complex structure and unique characteristics of cascode GaN devices, the traditional gate driver cannot satisfy or take the full advantage of the cascode GaN. This paper presents a SPICE modeling method that takes into account circuit layout and device parasitic to analyze switching behavior under the gate driving parameters, then a gate driver(GD) is proposed, which consisting of separated turn on and turn off path by different flying capacitors and gate resistors to control gate loop impedances at different transient stage. Compare with the traditional gate driver, the proposed GD can accelerate the switching speed and suppress the overshoot, oscillation and electromagnetic interference (EMI) produced by high di/dt and dv/dt while reduce the power loss. The experiment validated the effectiveness of proposed GD.

articleTitle: Detuned Dual-Frequency Compensation for Wide Misalignment Tolerance in Inductive Power Transfer Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: In inductive power transfer systems, misalignment can lead to inconsistent output power. In this paper, a topology based on a primary-side detuned dual-frequency compensation circuit is proposed to provide consistent output characteristics over a wide misalignment range. The proposed topology constructs two intersecting power vs. coupling coefficient curves at two switching frequencies. The coupling coefficient range can be extended without increasing primary current and reactive power variability by changing the switching frequency at curve intersections. With this approach, the output power changes by only 10% over a 2.5:1 coupling coefficient range, and efficiency at low coupling can be improved. This means the proposed topology is more adaptive for misalignment. A 1500 W prototype has been prepared to verify the topology. Efficiency ranges from 86.8% to 94.5% over a coupling coefficient range from 0.14 to 0.35.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Logic Control Strategy of Substation Voltage in Urban Rail Flexible Traction Power Supply System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: The flexible traction power supply system (FTPSS) for urban rail adopts fully controlled voltage source converter (VSC) to replace the diode rectifier unit, which has the advantages of improving the power supply quality and controlling the DC voltage. However, the impact of VSC DC voltage variations on the performance of FTPSS is not fully understood. This paper established the AC/DC decoupling model of FTPSS and analyzed the different utilization paths of regenerative braking energy. On this basis, the relationship between droop slope and power flow is analyzed by simulation under different power and distance between trains. Subsequently, based on fuzzy logic control (FLC), an adaptive adjustment strategy of substation voltage considering the dynamic operation process of trains is proposed. This strategy actively cooperates with the energy distribution of each station by changing the droop slope, so as to reduce the energy provided by the urban power grid (Eacgridrec) and stabilize the network voltage. Finally, a simulation verification is carried out by a subway line, and the results show that compared with the constant voltage control, the proposed strategy can reduce the Eacgridrec by 5.57%, and reduce the voltage fluctuation by 156.5826V compared to the droop control.

articleTitle: An Improved Stacked Multicell Converter with Fault Tolerant Capability Using Finite-Control-Set Model Predictive Control
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: The stacked multicell (SMC) converter suffers from low-frequency voltage fluctuations in the neutral point (NP), which gets substantially larger at specific operating conditions and affects the safe operation of the converter. This paper proposes an improved SMC (ISMC) converter to cope with this shortcoming. A finite control set model predictive control (FCS-MPC) strategy is designed to accurately track the output current and voltage balancing across the flying capacitors (FC). With this strategy, a fault-tolerant ability of the proposed converter is also presented. A post-fault reconfiguration of the controller is proposed to achieve FC voltage balancing under bidirectional switch faults. Simulation results under steady-state, dynamic, and faulty operating conditions justify the feasibility of the proposed converter.

Author Keywords: finite control set model predictive control

articleTitle: Optimization of Frequency Jittering Parameters for Conducted EMI Suppression in Switching Mode Power Supplies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: Electromagnetic interference (EMI) is an inevitable problem in switching mode power supplies. Frequency jitter is one of ways for power converters to reduce conducted EMI without extra hardware cost. In this paper, based on the triangular frequency modulation, the effect of different frequency jittering parameters on both peak and average noise suppression is discussed, including modulation index and frequency deviation, looking for the optimal frequency jittering parameters to maximize the conducted EMI suppression. A simulation model of EMI receiver is built to accurately predict the EMI noise amplitude. With the simulation model, the EMI suppression degree under different frequency jittering parameters is studied. The results show that there is a trade-off between peak and average noise suppression. Then the optimal frequency jittering parameters can be determined. The validity of the proposed analysis is verified by the experimental results from a switching mode power supply.

articleTitle: Energy Management Strategy of Multiple Energy Storage Systems in Urban Railway Based on Train Operating Status
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: With the rapid development of urban rail transit, installing multiple sets of ground energy storage devices on a line can help reduce train operation energy consumption and solve the problem of regeneration failure. In this paper, through typical operating scenarios of two energy storage systems and a single train, the impact of the no-load voltage difference of the substation on the charging and discharging of energy storage is analyzed, and an energy management strategy of multiple energy storage systems in urban railway based on train operating status is proposed. When the train is in traction, the charging and discharging threshold is increased to make the energy storage discharge in time. Finally, the simulation results under the parameters of the Beijing subway line are given. Compared with the traditional threshold method based on no-load voltage, the energy saving rate and voltage stabilization rate of the strategy proposed in this paper are effectively improved.

articleTitle: Deep Analysis and Comparison Study of Solid-State Circuit Breakers for DC Microgrid Protection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: Future energy systems face the fast growth of direct current (DC) in renewable power generation, energy storage, and loads. DC microgrids indicate a promising solution for efficiency, reliability and low cost to accommodate renewable energy and energy storage. Safety is considered the priority to be investigated since the industry currently lacks standards in DC fault detection and protection. DC does not show zero-crossing leading to difficulty for circuit-breaking high current. The paper focuses on the technology and studies the latest development of protection devices, mainly the solid-state circuit breakers for DC applications. The classification, simulation, and comparison presented in this paper are valuable leading to further research and development of the state-of-art protection devices that support the trend of DC microgrids.

articleTitle: A Novel and Robust Security Approach for Authentication, Integrity, and Confidentiality of Lithium-ion Battery Management Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: Battery management systems (BMSs) play a critical and crucial role in ensuring the safety and the efficiency of the batteries. The increasing BMS complexity, the expanding interconnections between batteries and applications, and the introduction of cloud-based energy storage system structures have led to growing concerns about battery cybersecurity. For instance, the data exchange between the local and remote BMS parts can be exposed to cybersecurity attacks. Classic BMSs are not equipped with security mechanisms that are instead essential to protect their integrity and reliability and prevent serious consequences such as loss of data, equipment damage, and counterfeiting of battery components. This work highlights the importance of securing BMSs against cyber threats and discusses the current state of the art of cybersecurity in BMSs. The main outcome is the proposal of a novel and robust security approach to design a BMS able to prevent misuse and undesired manipulation of battery equipment and data. The proposed design approach can be used as enabling technology to support the application to the BMSs of the most diffused security mechanisms adopted by the state of the art as cybersecurity protections.

articleTitle: A Self-Powered Sensing System with Embedded TinyML for Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: In the coming Industry 4.0 era, IoT (Internet of Things) technology plays a more and more critical role. Anomaly detection is one of the essential applications for ensuring safe manufacturing, living, etc. It equips the machine with intelligence for perceiving its situation in real-time to prevent disastrous breakdown. Such monitoring systems were usually based on commercial inertial measurement units (IMU) and artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms that run on resource-rich, power-hungry servers, causing a certain amount of energy for sensing and data transmitting. In this paper, we introduce a novel self-powered sensing system with tiny machine learning (Tiny ML) technique for anomaly detection. A lightweight piezoelectric self-powered sensor (SPS) is utilized to substitute the IMU. The system runs on a low-cost embedded system, realizing the low-power in-situ inferring. A rich dataset has been collected on a vibration platform and analyzed by six well-known machine-learning models. A compressed deep neuron network (DNN) with three hidden layers achieves an accuracy of 97.6 % given only 8-point normalized SPS data. The TinyML model is then deployed on embedded systems for on-device inferring and condition-based monitoring. Power measurement is conducted to compare the systems based on an IMU and an SPS. It has shown that the proposed self-powered sensing approach can save up to 66.74% of energy. The system provides a valuable reference for realizing pervasive sensing and ubiquitous AI.

articleTitle: Leveraging Deep Learning and Digital Twins to Improve Energy Performance of Buildings
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: Digital transformation in buildings accumulates massive operational data, which calls for smart solutions to utilize these data to improve energy performance. This study has proposed a solution, namely Deep Energy Twin, for integrating deep learning and digital twins to better understand building energy use and identify the potential for improving energy efficiency. Ontology was adopted to create parametric digital twins to provide consistency of data format across different systems in a building. Based on created digital twins and collected data, deep learning methods were used for performing data analytics to identify patterns and provide insights for energy optimization. As a demonstration, a case study was conducted in a public historic building in Norrköping, Sweden, to compare the performance of state-of-the-art deep learning architectures in building energy forecasting.

articleTitle: SAGPCN: Self-Attention Graph Pooling Convolutional Network for Battery State of Health Estimation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are widely applied in sustainable energy conversion system. Consequently, it is of great research significance to accurately estimate the state of health (SOH) of batteries. To effectively model the input features at the spatial level, this article proposes a self-attention graph pooling convolutional network (SAGPCN) to estimate the SOH. The advantages of SAGPCN proposed in this paper can be reflected as follows: (1) The SAGPCN can consider node characteristics and graph topology, which focuses the attention on key parts of the graph. (2) The SAGPCN designs a self-attention mechanism to reserve significant nodes and delete secondary nodes, so as to optimize the network structure. A real-world dataset is adopted to evaluate the proposed battery SOH estimation approach in this paper. Experimental results represent that the estimation performance of the proposed SAGPCN is better than some data-driven SOH prediction approaches.

articleTitle: Heuristic Energy Management Algorithm for Buildings with Renewables and Vehicle-to-Grid Charging
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: Electrical energy consumption is steadily growing worldwide, while renewable energy sources are gaining market share. In parallel, energy systems are undergoing a profound transformation, moving from a top-down hierarchical structure to a more decentralized model focused on the consumer, who will also produce, store and sell their own energy. This paper proposes a decision algorithm designed to help with the energy management task, in the context of a grid-connected household, with renewable energy production and electric vehicles (EVs). The algorithm makes use of several inputs such as energy consumption prediction, energy production output, EV battery state, and grid energy price in order to perform the optimal charge and discharge actions. The proposed algorithm was validated in a simulated environment attaining an average decrease of 18.9% in the energy cost of the household.

articleTitle: A P-Value Approach for Real-Time Identifying the Capacity Regeneration Phenomenon of Lithium-ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are favored as the primary energy storage option as a result of their high energy density, extended cycle life, and low self-discharge rate. However, the health condition of LIBs is critical for ensuring the overall safety, reliability, and optimal performance of electric vehicles (EV s) and other energy storage systems. The capacity regeneration phenomenon (CRP) causes an increase in the available capacity of LIBs during random periods of inactivity caused by variability in human behavior, such as the driving habits of EVs. The presence of CRP can have a significant impact on the accuracy of the state-of-health (SOH) estimation and the remaining useful life (RUL) prediction that most researchers often neglect, resulting in flawed SOH estimation, premature replacement, or unexpected battery failures. Therefore, developing accurate and reliable SOH estimation algorithms that consider various operating conditions and degradation mechanisms is crucial to ensure the optimal performance, reliability, and longevity of LIBs. This paper proposes a statistical approach using hypothesis testing and a test statistic with corresponding p-value that can effectively identify CRP in real time with 99.4 % accuracy.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Based Energy Management System for Renewable Energy Communities
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: Energy systems are under a profound transformation powered by the increasing penetration of renewable energy sources and the decentralization of electricity markets into local communities, in which the prosumer plays a fundamental role. As a result, the creation of Renewable Energy Communities (RECs) is becoming popular, especially in Europe, allowing their members to reduce electricity consumption from non-renewables, as well as to locally produce, store and exchange energy among themselves. This work introduces a REC management system using Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning (AI/ML) techniques for the electricity consumption forecast. The obtained results of the simulated scheme show that, with the use of these techniques, the system is able to decrease the electricity bill of the REC as well as the energy consumption from the distribution grid.

articleTitle: Construction and Application of Comprehensive Evaluation System for Layout Optimization of Super High-Rise Buildings Under Health Orientation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: With China's “healthy urbanization” concept and the strategic development of “dual carbon” healthy and intelligent buildings, traditional super high-rise buildings have insufficient design in terms of public health and eco-sustainability. According to the research basis of health-related standards and HIA-based research, starting from key points of the overall framework of architectural scheme design and the space requirements of active health, through the AHP-matter-element extension analysis method, the perspective of urban, architectural and physical elements based on the principle of health-oriented optimization is constructed. The layout design optimization factor evaluation system and the construction of a comprehensive evaluation model provide a good evaluation method and basis for the health-oriented optimization of the general layout of super high-rise buildings in the future.

articleTitle: Sustainable World with SCAP, DWPT and IWM: ~ Paradigm shift to Motor / Capacitor / Wireless ~
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: What will cars look like in 100 years' later? They must run by “electric motor” and will receive energy directly from electric power infrastructure like electric trains. The key technologies here are “supercapacitors” to excel in power input and output rather than batteries, and “wireless power transfer” to connect cars to power infrastructure. Furthermore, energy efficiency and safety will be dramatically improved by the technology of “motion control” to make use of the excellent torque control characteristics of electric motor, also together with automatic driving technology.

articleTitle: A Fault Diagnosis Method for Multilevel Inverters Based on Parallel Computing Architecture
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: Cascaded H-bridge multilevel inverter (CHMLI) is currently one of the most promising medium-high power grid connected inverter topologies. As the number of CHMLI power switch tubes increases, more computing resources are needed for the training and decision-making of power switch tube fault diagnosis, which aggravates the impact of faults. Therefore, it is urgent to develop a more rapid fault diagnosis computing architecture. To solve these problems, a parallel computing architecture based fault diagnosis method for multilevel inverters is proposed, which utilizes the parallel computing advantages of memristor cross arrays to improve the diagnostic efficiency of traditional methods. In this method, the output phase voltage of the inverter system is selected as the input signal of fault diagnosis. After data preprocessing, the weight storage and parallel calculation are carried out through the memristor cross arrays, and then the fault classification results are obtained through full connection. Compared with traditional methods, the proposed fault diagnosis method has advantages such as parallel computing, storage and fusion, and has shorter diagnosis time while ensuring diagnostic accuracy. Experimental results show that the proposed method is fast, effective and accurate.

articleTitle: Analysis of Power Grid Operation Characteristics with Distributed Generation Access Based on Data Mining
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: With the increasingly problems of environmental pollution and energy shortage, new energy power generation technology has been developed rapidly. The scale of grid-connected new energy generation in the distribution network is increasing, and its influence on the grid is becoming more and more significant, which also brings challenges to the system scheduling. Based on the historical data, after preprocessing a large number of data, the improved K-means clustering algorithm based on GSA elbow criterion is proposed to extract and mine the features of power data. On this basis, the output characteristics of new energy and regional load characteristics are analyzed. Secondly, the impact of distributed new energy on the peak-valley difference of load and the impact of new energy with different permeability on the system reserve are studied. Finally, the impact on the typical operation characteristics of regional power grid is analyzed.

articleTitle: Supercapacitors with Polymer Electrolyte and Shochu Waste as Carbon Electrode
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: Electric double-layer capacitors (EDLCs) are high-speed chargeable/dischargeable devices. The commercialization of this technology is hindered by the unavailability of inexpensive electrode materials. In this study, we present low-cost activated carbon electrodes fabricated from used shochu waste, and analyze their surface and electrochemical characteristics for the first time. We then determine the optimal time and temperature required for the activation of the KOH-CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> double-step reactions. Additionally, the obtained shochu waste carbons (SWCs) are used as the carbon electrodes of EDLCs, whose half-cell capacitances are evaluated using cyclic voltammetry. Their electrolyte and charge transfer resistances are estimated by measuring the corresponding AC impedance under both non-aqueous and aqueous electrolytes. The withstand voltage of the aqueous electrolyte is approximately 1.2 V, which is the voltage at which the electrolysis of water occurs; however, it lacks sufficient energy density. Therefore, we added sodium polyacrylate to the electrolyte to gelatinize it and prevent electrolysis, thereby improving the withstand voltage up to 3.5 V and obtained an energy density of 4.6 Wh/kg.

articleTitle: Evaluation Method of Residential Air Conditioning Load Time Series Adjustment Potential Based on Data Mining
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: Due to the diversity of air conditioning load types and the decentralized access points, it is challenging to conduct direct dispatching control. This paper discusses the exploration of air conditioner load response potential. Firstly, the K-means clustering algorithm is utilized to obtain the typical daily residential air conditioning load curve, and then the period is divided based on the characteristics of residential electricity consumption. Subsequently, a multi-period analysis model of air conditioning load during each key period is established using curve fitting technology, and a multi-period evaluation model of adjustable air conditioning load capacity considering multiple factors in residential areas is obtained. Finally, the effectiveness and applicability of this method are verified by using actual data.

articleTitle: Energy Trading Platform Research of Wire/wireless Vehicle-to-vehicle Energy Transfer Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: Electric vehicles have become an ultimate policy option to mitigate climate change, but there are major barriers in the scale of market diffusion. One of the key factors that lead to this is consumers' range anxiety. Several reasons cause the range anxiety such as EV range limited, charging time long and complicated, charging stations and supporting equipment insufficient,etc. Also, the low stability of EV battery is a concern for EV users. A framework of the V2V trading provides alternative EV charging infrastructures and significantly reduces range anxiety of EV users. EV users not only enjoy the convenient service of charging anytime and anywhere, but also make profits in the process of energy sharing. The proposed trading mechanism is validated using real-life EVs data of Shenzhen, one of cities with the highest EV penetration. In the future, V2V technology is promising to act as a key role in the electrification and decarbonisation of transportation.

articleTitle: Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning for Charging Coordination of Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: Virtual power plant (VPP) is a power system control center that mediates among the energy market, power grid, distributed energy resources, power storage units, controllable power loads, and electric vehicles (EV s), As energy consumers and wireless communication users, an EV is one of the key components of VPP systems that pose stringent requirements on both charging system management and communication infrastructure. On one hand, the optimal power flow (OPF) needs to minimize power system loss and voltage variance. On the other hand, communication quality of service (QoS) needs to be accounted for, in terms of data rate and latency in VPP systems. These lead long-term spatial EV charging coordination (i.e., charging station (CS) selection) a non-convex optimization problem, which is yet an open issue. In this regard, by embedding SG millimeter-wave (mm W) access point (AP) into CS, an AP-enabled CS architecture is first devised in this paper to support VPP control information flow and EV communication applications, such as autonomous driving. Based on the AP-enabled CS, an AP-enabled-CS-assisted multi-agent deep reinforcement learning algorithm (ABC-MADRL) is proposed to provide an intelligent long-term EV charging coordination solution. Experimental results illustrate that ABC-MADRL dramatically reduces the power loss and voltage variance by 24.3%, compared to the uncoordinated charging.

articleTitle: Explainable Transformer Model for Short-Term Wind Forecast
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: Short-term wind field forecasting, particularly wind speed prediction, is a critical component in wind farm control. Traditional statistical techniques, such as autoregressive integrated moving average, and machine learning approaches, such as recurrent neural networks, have been widely used for short-term forecasting, but these methods are often difficult to interpret. In this study, we propose a transformer model that can capture the internal dependencies within previous wind measurements to predict wind speeds in the upcoming hours. Measurement data from the FINO1 research platform collected in 2007 and 2008, including wind speeds, direction, and air temperature at three altitudes (40m, 60m, and 80m), have been used to train and evaluate the model. With the help of the attention mechanism in the transformer model, we can interpret the impact of the previous wind profile on future predictions, thereby enabling the explanation of deep learning models for wind forecasting. Our experimental results on the FINO1 measurement data demonstrate exceptional performance of the proposed model in short-term wind forecasting.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control of Five-Level Current Source Converter with Optimized Weighting Factors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: This paper presents the finite control set model predictive control (FCS-MPC) with improved control objectives using optimized weighting factors. The Pareto curve obtained from the Particle Swarm optimizes the weighting factors. The optimal weighting factors are then used in the FCS-MPC algorithm to enhance the control objective performance of a three-phase five-level current source converter (5L-CSC). In 5L-CSC, two identical three-level CSC (3L-CSC) modules are connected in parallel with one common current source supply to provide uniform five-level output current waveform. This CSC requires a current balance to operate the converter safely. Therefore, the control objective of the MPC is to control the output voltage and balance the internal currents. The weighting factors are optimized based on the converter's total harmonics distortion (THD) performance and inductor current ripple. The performance enhancement of 5L-CSC, utilizing optimal weighting factors, is confirmed through MATLAB simulations when compared to the model employing arbitrarily assigned weighting factors. The simulation outcomes additionally indicate that the integration of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) with FCS-MPC exhibits resilience across various condition settings.

Author Keywords: Finite Control Set Model Predictive Control

articleTitle: Adaptive Inertia Based on Secondary Control Strategy for VSGs with the SOC Constraint of DC-Side Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: The virtual synchronous generator (VSG) can provide inertia to the system, and effectively support the system frequency. However, the VSG inertia setting is subject to the physical limitations of the DC side, which cannot be changed arbitrarily. Aimed at this deficiency, this paper proposes a VSG inertia adaptive control strategy based on hybrid energy storage system (HESS). Based on the traditional inertia adaptive control, this strategy second adjusts the virtual inertia according to the state of charge (SOC) of the supercapacitor (SC), which can not only prevent the SC from overcharge and overdischarge, but also improve the frequency characteristics of VSG in the transient process. Finally, the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed strategy are verified by comparing the control effects of different VSG strategies through Matlab/Simulink simulation.

articleTitle: Capacity Configuration Method of Urban Rail Energy Storage System Based on NSGA-II and Simplified Energy Storage Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: The electricity consumption of urban rail transit increases year by year with its rapid development. The regenerative braking energy generated by the train can be absorbed and reused by the ground energy storage systems, which can effectively reduce the traction energy consumption, so as to achieve the goal of low carbon and energy saving. It is necessary to consider how to configure its capacity. At present, ground energy storage systems mostly use intelligent algorithms for capacity configuration. Although this method improves the speed and accuracy of capacity configuration, it is essentially a fast traversal of the precise model. Although the number of traversals is reduced, due to the large scale of the precise model of the traction power supply system, the single solution speed is very slow, and its configuration efficiency is still not high. In this paper, on the premise that the substation energy can flow in both directions, the obtained substation rectification and inverter power curve is divided according to the power and capacity of the energy storage systems to be configured, so as to estimate the loss value of the braking resistor of the precise model, which improves the single solution speed, saving capacity configuration time. Taking a domestic subway line as an example, using the Elitist Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm (NSGA-II) to solve a simplified energy storage model based on the division of rectifier and inverter power curves to determine the capacity configuration scheme can improve the efficiency of energy storage capacity configuration.

articleTitle: Study of a Aggregated Baseline Load Forecasting Method Based on Decoupling of Distributed PV-Containing Customers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: In recent years, the distributed PV industry has developed rapidly, and more and more residential customers have started to install distributed PV power generation systems, while the unobservable characteristics of behind-the-meter distributed PV bring great challenges to the demand response aggregated baseline load (ABL) prediction. To improve the one-inch accuracy of ABL under high penetration distributed PV, a aggregated baseline load forecasting method based on decoupling of distributed PV-containing customers is proposed. Firstly, the abnormal load data is identified and corrected based on t-test in mathematical statistics, and the temperature data is corrected; secondly, a PV user identification method based on weather state characteristics is used to separate PV users and non-PV users; then, the aggregated baseline load of non-PV users is predicted by considering the differentiation of users' electricity consumption patterns; again, the aggregated baseline load for PV users is classified by typical weather types and a prediction model is built for each weather type using SVR for aggregated baseline load prediction; finally, the predicted values for both types of users are combined to obtain the final ABL prediction values. The simulation results show that the proposed method reduces the average absolute error index by 2.65 and the root mean square error index by 0.76 on average compared with the direct prediction method and other classification prediction methods.

articleTitle: Application of Stochastic Averaging to Vibrating Electro-mechanical Systems for Piezoelectric Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
abstract: Electro-mechanical systems are ubiquitous in engineering. For example, they are used in energy harvesting systems to convert random mechanical excitations into usable electrical power. The analysis and design of these electro-mechanical systems is particularly challenging, because concepts and methods of stochastic analysis and nonlinear dynamics are required. In this work we present a methodology for the analysis of nonlinear electro-mechanical systems with small internal friction, and subject to random external mechanical excitations. The method is based on the combined application of a model order reduction technique, to reduce the number of dynamical variables, thus reducing the complexity, and of stochastic averaging, to calculate statistical relevant quantities, and in particular expectations of the output electrical variables. As an example, we apply the proposed technique to the analysis of a piezoelectric energy harvesting system.
